messages:
maria: Quick announce — we just finished a staged canary for a new runtime change called 'adaptive warmup prefetch' and the early results look solid :tada:

maria: Summary numbers (canary vs baseline): p50 latency -7.8%, p99 latency -3.1%, token unit cost -5.9%. throughput stable.

maria: High level: the change does lightweight speculative KV prefetch + short-token warmup for likely continuations predicted by the seq-estimator. It prefers low-overhead heuristics for short/interactive requests to avoid batching blowups.

maria: Config we toggled on canary (for reference):

```yaml
prefetch:
  mode: adaptive-warmup
  lookahead_k: 8
  budget_tokens_per_req: 64
  throttle_pct: 10
```

maria: Observations: small memory delta (~+2% KV memory p95 on the canary fleet) and no increase in tail OS scheduling. No downstream error spike.

aj: Nice. Did you see any change to cold-starts for long-context jobs?

maria: Good q — long-context sequential jobs actually saw slightly better p50 because KV priming avoids a couple expensive kernel paths early. Cold GPU init unaffected.

devin: Is this opt-out-able per model? We need to keep some evals deterministic.

maria: Yes — per-model flag: `prefetch.warmup.enabled=false`. Also can be turned off per-route from Console.

sam: Where's the dashboard? want to bookmark the graphs.

maria: Internal dash: https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/2490012345 (canary cohort deck). I put p50/p99/cost charts and the request-slices we used.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed on cohort A (40 hosts). No alerts.

nick: Please add a short blurb to release-notes and let CS know about the cost delta so they can update pricing experiments.

maria: Will do. Plan: ramp to Dedicated lanes over 48h, keep canary metrics on for 7 days, escalate if p99 regresses >5% from baseline. Ping @oncall if anomalies.

aj: Nice win — will test with the summarization workload tomorrow.

maria: Thanks all — if you see anything odd, drop it here. :thumbsup:
